summary: You delivered a well-conceived Australian reef-monitoring mission concept with strong STK access analysis in your ground segment and a thorough introduction. To advance your mission design to a professional standard, focus on refining orbital mechanics fundamentals (such as retrograde launch dynamics), providing supporting hand calculations, eliminating design contradictions regarding maneuvers, and adhering to formal academic reporting standards with proper figure numbering and peer-reviewed citations.
next_steps: Recalculate your launch delta-v budget to correctly account for the Earth rotational velocity penalty when launching into retrograde sun-synchronous inclinations from equatorial sites.
Supplement your STK simulation outputs with independent hand calculations for parameters like orbital period, coverage revisit rates, or aerodynamic drag decay timelines.

Standardise your report presentation by numbering all figure captions, completing truncated text in the EOL section, and replacing non-academic references like Wikipedia with peer-reviewed literature.

criteria.C1: You clearly established ZYZZsat's primary reef-monitoring mission, justified a single satellite, and identified key stakeholders like CSIRO and BOM in the Introduction. To reach the top of Accomplished, integrate deeper literature citations connecting your mission requirements directly to existing Australian Earth-observation and reef-monitoring frameworks.
criteria.C2: You effectively applied STK to assess Mt Pleasant access and selected an appropriate 600 km SSO. To achieve Accomplished, correct technical misconceptions—such as the velocity penalty when launching retrograde orbits from equatorial sites—resolve contradictions between active maneuvers and passive drag deorbit, and support software models with hand calculations.
criteria.C3: Your conclusion provides a solid synthesis of the mission architecture and astutely highlights programmatic risks, such as Vega E development status. To achieve the top mark in Accomplished, include more detailed, quantitative conclusions evaluating whether the final orbital elements and revisit intervals fully satisfy the initial science goals.
criteria.C4: The report features a logical structure and concise executive summary. To achieve Accomplished, number and caption all figures formally, proofread to fix incomplete sentences (such as in Mission Duration & EOL), and ensure your bibliography uses professional reference styles rather than bare URLs or Wikipedia citations.
